jobConfig.name: S3_RAW_CLEAN_sPARK
jobConfig.description: Cleaning the quoted newline issue within the column "Storelocation" causing the reader to put it on a new line

script:
"""
AWS Glue ETL Job: Fix multi-line CSV fields and convert to Parquet
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose:
  Reads raw CSV data from S3 where quoted fields (e.g. StoreLocation)
  contain embedded newlines, which breaks Athena's default row-splitting
  behavior. Uses Spark's native multiLine CSV reader to parse it correctly,
  then writes the cleaned data out as Parquet to a new S3 location.

How to use:
  1. In AWS Glue Console -> ETL jobs -> Create job -> Spark
  2. Paste this script in (or upload as the job script)
  3. Update the SOURCE_PATH and TARGET_PATH constants below
  4. Set the job parameter --JOB_NAME when running
  5. Attach an IAM role with read access to SOURCE_PATH and write access
     to TARGET_PATH
  6. After the job succeeds, create/update your Glue Catalog table (or run
     a crawler) pointed at TARGET_PATH, using the Parquet SerDe
"""

import sys
from awsglue.transforms import *
from awsglue.utils import getResolvedOptions
from pyspark.context import SparkContext
from awsglue.context import GlueContext
from awsglue.job import Job
from pyspark.sql.functions import regexp_replace, col

# ---- CONFIG: update these for your environment ----
SOURCE_PATH = "s3://roshan-de-practice-2026/Raw__data/"
TARGET_PATH = "s3://roshan-de-practice-2026/clean-parquet/"
COLUMNS_TO_CLEAN = ["StoreLocation"]  # columns that may contain embedded newlines

# ---- Job boilerplate ----
args = getResolvedOptions(sys.argv, ['JOB_NAME'])
sc = SparkContext()
glueContext = GlueContext(sc)
spark = glueContext.spark_session
job = Job(glueContext)
job.init(args['JOB_NAME'], args)

# ---- Read raw CSV ----
# multiLine=True tells Spark's CSV reader to treat a quoted field's embedded
# newline as part of the value, not as a row break -- this is the fix for
# the "COLUMN_NOT_FOUND" / row-splitting issue seen in Athena.
df = (
    spark.read
    .option("multiLine", "true")
    .option("header", "true")
    .option("quote", '"')
    .option("escape", '"')
    .csv(SOURCE_PATH)
)

# ---- Clean up columns with embedded newlines ----
for column_name in COLUMNS_TO_CLEAN:
    if column_name in df.columns:
        df = df.withColumn(column_name, regexp_replace(col(column_name), "\n", ", "))

# ---- Sanity check (shows up in Glue job logs / CloudWatch) ----
row_count = df.count()
print(f"Row count after clean read: {row_count}")
df.show(5, truncate=False)

# ---- Write out as Parquet ----
# Parquet avoids this entire class of row/column-splitting problem going
# forward, and gives you real typed columns instead of everything-as-string.
(
    df.write
    .mode("overwrite")
    .parquet(TARGET_PATH)
)

job.commit()
